contract.sync_assumed: warp convergence of the 32 lanes, the caller separates calls that reuse the output buffer by a __syncwarp (the harness does)
contract.sync_performed: one redux.sync per round plus one redux.max (fp32 next-word check) over the full warp mask, no barriers, no shared memory
contract.k_range: [1, N/2], measured 4 to 1024, k above 64 runs the rounds as a rolled loop
contract.n_range: N = 32 x IPT, power of two, measured 32 to 2048 (N 4096 at k 4 to 64 built but not yet measured, its k 256 and 1024 translation units compile for over 20 minutes)
contract.type_constraints: bf16 (16 twiddled key bits above a 16-bit inverted index, exact) and fp32 (top 32 - log2 N twiddled key bits above the index, idea N4, exact after the tie pass), int32 indices derived from the position
contract.nan_behavior: a NaN with the sign bit clear twiddles above +inf and is selected first, a NaN with the sign bit set is never selected, the all-ones pattern may collide with the empty-list sentinel, focus-set inputs contain no NaN
contract.tie_break_support: inherent: the packed word orders by (key descending, index ascending), prefer_smaller_index runs the same code and measured identical to not_guaranteed in every cell (124 vs 124 at N 32 k 4 bf16 up to 150107 vs 150109 at N 2048 k 1024)
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: slot r holds the r-th largest key, ties by smaller index (the fp32 tie pass may reorder the last slots of the tie class)

correctness.notes: oracle battery passed on all 40 cells. This batch ran twice on the node 43 seconds apart (state/results/opt-W2/..._135810.json and ..._135853.json, same holder, same container, both under the GPU lock), the card uses the second, the two agree to the cycle in latency and within 1.2 percent in throughput.

low_level: The next-word check replaces the per-item count of v1 by one more redux after the rounds: fp32 N 256 k 8 has 11 CREDUX (8 rounds, 1 check, 2 in the slow path that never runs) and 416 SASS instructions against 400 for v1's throughput kernel, but the register allocator no longer provisions the v1 count path and the throughput kernel drops from 56 to 40 registers at N 256 (occupancy 4 to 6 blocks per SM), 96 to 64 at N 512 (2 to 4), 172 to 115 at N 1024 k 16 (1 to 2).

Latency kernel registers also fall (fp32 N 512 k 16: 104 to 69, N 1024 k 16: 168 to 128) and the 56-byte spill of v1 at N 1024 k 16 is gone, but new spills appear at N 1024 k 32 (20 bytes) and N 2048 k 4 to 16 (160 to 232 bytes against 0 to 56 for v1), where the slow path's twiddled-key and member arrays (IPT entries each) are provisioned in the latency kernel's longer live range.

bf16 cells compile to the same code in v1 and v2 (the policy only changes the fp32 tie pass) and measure identical to the cycle in all 20 bf16 cells, which doubles as an A/A noise reference for the batch: 0 cycles of latency difference, throughput within 1 percent.
Fits R squared 1.0000, canary 32.001 cycles per op at start and end, node umbriel-b200-047.
algorithmic: The fp32 overhead over bf16 at the same cell drops from 234 to 304 cycles (v1) to 80 to 115 cycles at N 256 (k 8: 463 against 365, k 16: 682 against 602, k 32: 1115 against 1000) and to 77 at N 1024 k 16 (1684 against 1607), which is the N4 card's modeled constant (about 150) or better. Gains over v1: 1.45x at N 256 k 4, 1.30x at k 8 and 16, 1.85x at N 512 k 4, 1.35x at N 512 k 8, 1.44x at N 1024 k 4, 1.21x at N 1024 k 16, shrinking to 1.02 to 1.08x at k 32 and 64 where the rounds dominate.
Throughput gains follow the occupancy: 1.20 to 1.26x at N 256 to 512 for k 4 to 8, 1.13 to 1.18x at k 16, 1.40x at N 1024 k 64 (occupancy 1 to 2).

The check is exact: the largest word not emitted is max over lanes of max(list head, spare), where spare is the largest word each lane dropped in its top-L prologue merge, tracked with one extra min and max per merged item. A tie-class member was left out exactly when that word shares the truncated key of the k-th word. The oracle battery (tie_heavy, pivot_tie, all_equal, quantized patterns force the slow path) passed on every cell.
negative: Three fp32 cells got slower: N 1024 k 8 (1902 against 1407, 0.74x), N 2048 k 16 (4594 against 3907, 0.85x) and N 2048 k 32 (6842 against 5688, 0.83x), with N 2048 k 8 flat. The slow path keeps IPT twiddled keys and IPT member flags live from the check to the end, and at IPT 32 to 64 the compiler either spills them (N 2048) or schedules the prologue around them (N 1024 k 8 at 104 registers, no spill, still 500 cycles slower). Making the slow path recompute from the keys (or reload them) instead of materializing the arrays is the fix to try, not measured.
The spare tracking costs one VIMNMX pair per merged item, visible at N 2048 (1029 VIMNMX against about 960) but not in the bf16 numbers since bf16 does not track it.
surprises: Removing the count loop cut registers by a third even though the slow path still references every key: the compiler provisions registers for the hot path's live ranges and the v1 count was hot.

fp32 at N 256 k 4 to 16 is now within 80 to 115 cycles of bf16 on a round structure that is identical, so the remaining fp32 cost is the wider prologue (32-bit twiddle and pack against the 16-bit shift and or) plus one redux.
open_questions: The three regressed cells: whether an outlined slow path (noinline function taking the keys by reference) or a reload of the keys from the input pointer removes the provisioned arrays.

Whether the spare tracking can be dropped by emitting k + 1 rounds (the (k+1)-th word is then the next word for free) at one extra round of 25 cycles, which also removes the min and max per merged item.
